newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO denies leaving weapons outside Karadzic base.
newsitem.headline: NATO denies leaving weapons outside Karadzic base.

text.p: NATO officers denied on Friday that peacekeeping troops had left their assault weapons behind when entering the base of war crimes indictee Radovan Karadzic to meet Bosnian Serb leaders.
One official told Reuters any indication of Karadzic's presence in the building during Thursday's meeting were at best "circumstantial".

NATO commander Admiral Joseph Lopez joined peace coordinator Carl Bildt and other officials at the meeting with acting Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic to discuss security arrangements for Saturday's elections.
Her offices are in the same factory complex which Bosnian Serb ex-president Karadzic uses as his working headquarters.
Some reporters heard U.S. soldiers in Lopez's security detail agree to a Serb police request not to carry automatic rifles inside the factory complex.

But officers in the NATO force, which is sensitive to accusations that it knows where indicted Serb separatist war criminals are but goes out of its way to avoid them, strongly denied Lopez's bodyguards had agreed to this.

"Yes, the Serbs did ask us (not to bring assault weapons into the complex) and I believe the response was 'Stuff it' or words to that effect," Major Brett Boudreau, spokesman for the peace Implementation Force (IFOR), told a news briefing.

"The fact is, we went into the (complex) with our long barrelled weapons to guard Lopez and Bildt there. But we did not bring them into Mrs Plavsic's office (building) as a courtesy. We did bring our pistols as a matter of security."
NATO troops are under orders to arrest war crimes indictees should they encounter them in the course of their normal duties, but they have refused to stage manhunts.
Karadzic has been indicted by the international criminal tribunal on former Yugoslavia for crimes against humanity.
